summary: A first-person reflection on how healthcare employment has shifted since September 2023, told through the author's path from nursing graduate to healthcare policy advocate. It covers growth in telehealth, healthcare IT, genetics, personal care, mental health, care coordination, AI and policy roles, with quotes from professionals the author met. It also notes how education has adapted and expects employment trends to keep evolving.
one_line: A personal account of healthcare job trends since September 2023, spanning telehealth, IT, genetics, home care, mental health, AI and policy roles.
key_facts: The author began as a nursing graduate at a bustling city hospital and later became a healthcare policy advocate.
Dr. Eileen Carter, an internal medicine specialist the author shadowed, said in late fall last year: "Telehealth isn't just an alternative; it's a staple that is expanding our reach."
Telehealth jobs grew not only for clinicians but also for technicians, software developers and customer service professionals.
Sarah Ramirez, a former classmate, moved from nursing into healthcare information technology, citing a surge in demand around January 2024.
Sarah Ramirez's work includes troubleshooting EMR software, safeguarding patient data and training medical staff on digital tools.
MediTalent Inc., a recruitment firm specializing in healthcare placements, predicted growth in "digital care teams" where IT experts work in realtime with physicians.
James Patterson, a genetic counselor, spoke with the author in spring 2024 and called his work "personalized medicine at its best."
Maria Lopez, a recruiter for Comfort at Home Services, said that by mid-2024 her agency had doubled the number of carers it employs.
Michael Johnson, a clinical psychologist, saw his practice grow threefold and said in late 2024 that mental health access is "a health revolution as crucial as any vaccine."
Andrea Mitchell, a care coordinator at a multidisciplinary clinic, described her role as "part navigational officer, part detective."
Rajiv Singh, an AI healthcare consultant, showed the author how technical AI capabilities are aligned with the nuances of patient care.
The author completed a short course on healthcare informatics at the Clara Barton Nursing School in February 2025; its syllabus now includes advanced analytics and telehealth competency.
Advocacy for better working conditions, patient rights and accessible healthcare has increased jobs for legislative advisors and healthcare lobbyists.
